extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and applicants preparing NIH/NIAID grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers using NIAID sample applications to guide preparation and evaluation of NIH-style grant applications, with emphasis on Research Strategy, Specific Aims, reviewer criteria, and compliance with current application instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the NOFO/NOSI and SF 424 Application Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow the instructions in your chosen Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) or Notice of Special Interest (NOSI) and adhere to the latest NIH SF 424 Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample applications may not reflect the latest application format or rules, so it is critical to follow current official instructions rather than relying on older sample formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of Research Strategy and Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples provide examples of good grantsmanship and successful approaches to presenting a Research Strategy and Specific Aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample applications to learn structures, tone, level of detail, and organization that have led to successful reviews, but adapt to current instructions and the specifics of your project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (reviewer critique factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers critique applications on 'significance' — whether the project addresses an important problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing samples, note reviewer comments about significance to understand how applicants framed the importance and potential impact of their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (reviewer critique factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate 'innovation' — whether the project uses novel concepts, approaches, or challenges existing paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe how successful applicants highlighted novelty and differentiated their work from existing literature in sample applications and in reviewer feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (reviewer critique factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the 'approach' — the rigor, strategy, and feasibility of the proposed methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine reviewer comments on approach in samples to learn expectations about experimental design, methods rigor, contingency plans, and feasibility arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of research and relevance to public health
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how investigators describe their research and its relevance to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying samples, pay attention to how applicants connect their specific aims and strategy to broader public-health relevance and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and support provided by the applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe the evidence and support (e.g., preliminary data, rationale, citations) provided by applicants to justify the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use samples to see the kinds and amount of supporting data and argumentation that reviewers found persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate level of technicality and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the level of technicality used in explanations — balancing technical detail for expert reviewers with clear exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples illustrate how much technical detail to include and how to present complex methods or concepts clearly so reviewers can evaluate significance, innovation, and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and document formatting for assistive technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample applications have been reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare application documents with accessibility in mind (e.g., readable formatting, tagged PDFs) so materials are usable by all reviewers and comply with accessibility expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect confidential, commercial, and personal information in shared materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample applications include substantial redactions to protect confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sharing or using sample materials, recognize and respect redactions; applicants should likewise safeguard confidential or proprietary information when preparing submissions and when consenting to share materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare successful and unsuccessful examples and official writing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare NIAID sample applications with unsuccessful examples (e.g., National Institute on Aging K99/R00 samples) and with NIAID/NIH official guidance resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparisons between successful and unsuccessful applications and consult 'Apply for a Grant', 'Important Writing Tips', and 'Write Your Application' to identify concrete differences and improve grantsmanship.
